text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- MENEM REACTS TO NEW DECREE ON AUTOMOBILES

Argentine President Carlos Menem said Brazil's policy of granting special tax incentives to car makers building plants in the North, Northeast and Center-East of Brazil should not be valid indefinitely.
-- KOLYNOS TO BE OUT OF THE MARKET FOR 4 YRS
Kolynos toothpaste is likely to be out of the market for four years. This was the option chosen by Colgate-Palmolive to have the acquisition of Kolynos approved by Brazilian authorities.
-- CREDICARD NETS 250 MLN REAIS
Credicard S.A. is closing the year with a net profit of 250 million reais, an increase of 130 percent when compared with 1995.
-- BRAZIL POSTS RECORD BANKRUPTCY FILINGS
A total of 4,100 companies filed for bankruptcy between January and November, a rise of 71 percent when compared with the same period of last year.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- FEDERAL DEFICIT IS THE HIGHEST OF THE DECADE

The federal government's operational deficit between January and November rose to 1.78 percent of GDP from 1.64 percent in the same period of last year. The deficit was the highest of the decade. Federal expenses were 12.35 billion reais higher than the government's receipts.
-- CONGRESS TO VOTE TODAY ON RURAL TAX BILL
Lawmakers will vote today on a proposal creating a new tax on rural properties. Agrarian Reform Minister Raul Jungmann expects the approval even without the support of the rural bloc in Congress.
O GLOBO
-- GOV'T WILL PUNISH EXCESSIVE FUEL PRICES HIKES

The Brazilian government will punish distributors which raised fuel prices excessively. Gasoline prices were expected to rise between eight percent and ten percent, but prices rose above the government's estimates.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom, 55-11-2485412
